clue.text: Cook very sour northern delicacy

parts.note: to bake is to cook in an oven
well can mean very, as in 'well pleased'
tart means sharp or sour in taste

explanation.surface: Someone cooks a notably sour regional speciality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the instruction to an anagram, but it simply gives BAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bakewell tart is an almond and jam pastry named after Bakewell, a town in Derbyshire in the north of England.

clue.text: Black, freezing cold, the French boneshaker

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
freezing means icy
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A dark, frozen old French bicycle rattles along.
explanation.walkthrough: A boneshaker is the nickname for an early bicycle with solid tyres, so the definition is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Boneshaker is a nickname for an old bike with iron or solid tyres, giving a rough ride.

clue.text: Snorkel pipe blocked by seaweed

indicators.note: the answer is held inside the words, as if blocking the run of letters across them

explanation.surface: A diver's snorkel tube gets clogged with weed from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Kelp is a large brown species of seaweed.

clue.text: Bird and funny individual dog

parts.note: a wag is a joker, a funny person
to dog someone is to follow them, to tail them

explanation.surface: A bird and a comic character each have their own dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' reads as a noun but is the verb meaning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The wagtail is a small songbird known for bobbing its long tail.

clue.text: Article removed by paparazzo caught in Naples misbehaving

indicators.note: the letter for caught goes inside the rearranged city name
the letters of the city name behave badly and fall out of order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges NAPLES to LENSAP; 'in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographer takes the protective cover off the front of the camera lens before shooting.

clue.text: Picked up tie or gear for dancing

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the clue word's sense is said aloud

parts.note: a tie or draw in a game might be a score of two-two

explanation.surface: Someone chooses a tie or other clothing for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like choosing clothes; it signals that 'two-two', a drawn score, is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short stiff skirt worn by a ballerina.

clue.text: Exchange two cloths

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
lace is an openwork fabric

explanation.definitionFit: To exchange one thing for another is to substitute or swap it.

clue.text: Ban renegade dodgy American meat supplier

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or out of true, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An order to bar a crooked American who sells meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges BANRENEGADE into ABERDEENANG.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Scottish cattle breed raised for beef, so it supplies meat.

clue.text: Sweet new bride hung over — dress torn away at the top

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the first part sits above the second
new suggests the letters are made anew in a fresh order
the dress word loses its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: A newly married woman has a hangover, and her dress is ripped at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges BRIDEHUNG into EDINBURGH; 'torn away at the top' takes F from FROCK to leave ROCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh rock is a crumbly pastel-coloured Scottish confection, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Support Left over good work still to be done

parts.note: to back is to support
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Support anything left over from good work still to be done.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlog is an accumulation of tasks waiting to be finished.

clue.text: Mark flat jotter

parts.note: to note is to mark or observe
a pad is informal for a flat or home

explanation.surface: Mark rents a flat and keeps a notebook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but gives NOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A jotter is a small book of paper for writing notes.

clue.text: Risqué, timeless actor Spencer

indicators.note: time is abbreviated T, so without time means losing that letter

parts.note: Spencer Tracy was an American film actor

explanation.surface: A classic film star of the past is described as somewhat naughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something slightly indecent or sexually suggestive.

clue.text: Managed vacant Cornish farm

parts.note: ran means managed, as in running a business

indicators.note: vacant means emptied, keeping only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone ran an empty farm in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially for raising cattle.

clue.text: Youngster starts to feel awkward with nanny

indicators.note: the starts of the words, their first letters, are taken

explanation.surface: A child begins to feel shy with a new babysitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nanny' suggests a goat; here it only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fawn is a young deer, so it is a youngster of the animal world.

clue.text: Require broadcast work with dough

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out over the air, so the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to require is to need

explanation.surface: A request for broadcast work involving money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' suggests cash; here it is the baker's dough.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to press and fold bread mixture with the hands.

clue.text: Quick foray captures pawn

indicators.note: captures means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a foray is a raid
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A quick attack in chess that takes a pawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid is a synonym of quick or fast.

clue.text: Eagle, tern, albatross circling without end

indicators.note: the outer words surround the answer, which is concealed within them

explanation.surface: Seabirds wheel around the sky endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without end' looks like an instruction to drop a last letter, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal lasts forever and never finishes.

clue.text: "High table" dish, starter from Aston University

parts.note: a plate is a dish

indicators.note: the starter of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dish served at the high table of a university dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High table' sounds like a college dining table; it means a raised, flat area of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an elevated area of flat land, a kind of tableland.

clue.text: Provide commentary barking arrant nonsense at the end

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so the letters go wild
the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A commentator talks complete, utter nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' rearranges ARRANT into NARRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to give a spoken account of events, as a commentator does.

clue.text: Replay gag about Mike Atherton's debut

indicators.note: about means around, so one part is placed round the other

explanation.walkthrough: Mike Atherton is a former England cricket captain, which steers to cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A rematch is a second game between the same opponents, a replay.

clue.text: Sanction flying drones, the latest from Ukraine

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are moving about
the latest letter is the final one of the word

explanation.surface: A government approves drone flights and news from Ukraine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges DRONES into ENDORS.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to approve or authorise.

clue.text: Natter with boring mate back in snug

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

indicators.note: the back of the word is its last letter

clue.text: Freddie regularly visits downmarket eatery in the city

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'the city' is a vague definition; a caff is a cheap British cafe, and 'regularly' takes the even letters of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.

clue.text: We had to save balance, gained after a struggle

indicators.note: to save means to keep safe inside, so the balance word is enclosed

parts.note: we had contracts to we'd
the rest is the balance, the remainder

explanation.surface: A gymnast must save their balance, won after effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrested means seized or obtained with effort and force.

clue.text: Unfeeling note initially upset my brother

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each word

explanation.definitionFit: Numb means lacking sensation or emotion.

clue.text: Trouble in front of fleet deck

indicators.note: the trouble word comes before the fleet

explanation.surface: Trouble ahead of the ships on a deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a ship's deck but is the verb to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate or embellish.

clue.text: Shoulder or stomach

definitions.meaning: to shoulder a burden is to carry it
to stomach something is to tolerate it

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to carry or put up with something difficult.

clue.text: Ink manufacturer having month off work

indicators.note: off means removed, so the month is taken away

parts.note: an octopus squirts ink
Oct is short for October

explanation.surface: An ink company takes a month off work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ink manufacturer' suggests a company; it is the octopus.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary work.

clue.text: France given its island data

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
France's own word for island is ile

explanation.surface: France is given an island of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A file is a collection of data or records.

clue.text: Amphora (pot) put back outside, being of decent quality

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse order
the run of letters uses the outside ends of the first and last words, the answer lying within the phrase

explanation.surface: An ancient jar is put back outdoors, still in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Amphora (pot) put' backwards: TUPTOPAROHPMA holds the answer, spanning the end of 'put', all of 'pot' and the end of 'amphora'.

clue.text: Form of language mother shunned as foolish

indicators.note: shunned means avoided, so the mother word is left out

parts.note: idiomatic describes natural, idiom-based forms of language
ma is mother

explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means very stupid, foolish.

clue.text: Idler fetches fancy sofa

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate, so the letters are arranged in a new way
